title: Generate ObligationLedger 1.0 documents deterministically from task contract structured fields
objective: Implement a deterministic generator, exposed as a new CLI verb generate-ledger, that reads exactly one task contract JSON document and produces two output files: an unmodified-schema ObligationLedger 1.0 document, and a new LedgerGenerationReport 1.0 sidecar document carrying provenance and coverage. The generator's only obligation sources are the task contract's deliverables array and, whichever is present, its required_contract_decisions or required_invariants array; objective, acceptance_commands, and every other task-contract field are permanently excluded and never parsed for obligations. traceId is never inferred from the task contract; it is a required explicit CLI argument bound into the generated ledger. Stable obligation ids are a deterministic function of taskContractId, source field name, and source array index, so regenerating from byte-identical input is byte-reproducible. A task contract with zero usable structured entries across both source categories produces no output and a fail-closed diagnostic, never a fallback to free text. The generator emits signals: [] unconditionally and validates only ObligationLedgerValidator Phase A (ledger-only structural) rules before writing output; it never runs Phase B cross-document referential validation, since no trace envelope is paired at generation time, and it never attaches signals, integrates with AgentSession/GateOutcome, or invokes evaluate. Implement exactly the normative decisions fixed in docs/architecture/ADR-0007-task-contract-ledger-generation.md and docs/contracts/ledger-generation-report.md; do not reopen or reinterpret them.
depends_on: docs/architecture/ADR-0007-task-contract-ledger-generation.md must be approved and unmodified before implementation begins
phase-4-1-agent-session and phase-4-2-gate-outcome are complete; this task does not modify their contracts or integrate with them
required_contract_decisions: Scope is Narrow: the generator accepts only the existing tasks/*.json task contract document shape and makes no general document-to-obligation conversion claim.

The only obligation sources read from a task contract are deliverables and, whichever key is present, required_contract_decisions or required_invariants; if both are present and non-empty, both are read.
objective, acceptance_commands, and every other task-contract property are permanently excluded from obligation derivation; no free-text or semantic parsing of any kind is performed.

A task contract with zero usable candidate entries across both source categories produces no ledger and no report and fails closed with diagnostic PT603; it is never treated as vacuously valid and never falls back to objective.

Each obligation's stable id is exactly "<taskContractId>:<sourceField>:<index>", a pure function of the source document's own id, the source field name, and the zero-based array index of the contributing entry; the generator introduces no random or time-based identity.
traceId is supplied only as an explicit CLI argument, never inferred from the task contract or invented; a missing or empty traceId argument fails closed with diagnostic PT605.

Provenance and coverage are recorded only in a new, independently versioned LedgerGenerationReport 1.0 sidecar document; contracts/obligation-ledger.schema.json and docs/contracts/obligation-ledger.md receive zero diffs.

Coverage uses exactly the three closed statuses derived-automatic, manual, and unsupported-no-source-field, exactly as defined in docs/contracts/ledger-generation-report.md; the generator itself only ever emits derived-automatic on obligations and unsupported-no-source-field on the source-field list.

The generator emits signals: [] unconditionally, runs ObligationLedgerValidator Phase A before writing any output, and never runs Phase B; it does not attach signals, does not integrate with AgentSession or GateOutcome, and does not call evaluate.

The new generate-ledger CLI verb takes exactly four positional arguments (task-contract-path, trace-id, ledger-output-path, report-output-path), writes both output files only on full success, and reuses the existing 0/1/2 exit-code convention exactly as mapped in docs/contracts/ledger-generation-report.md.

Every fail-closed condition emits the exact diagnostic code and pointer fixed in docs/contracts/ledger-generation-report.md's diagnostic registry (PT600-PT606); no new code, pointer rule, or exit behavior is invented.
deliverables: LedgerGenerationReport 1.0 JSON Schema (contracts/ledger-generation-report.schema.json) matching this repository already-approved version, unmodified in shape

Deterministic ProgressTrace.Core.Generation namespace implementing task-contract structural reading, candidate extraction, stable-id computation, ledger assembly, Phase A validation reuse, and report assembly
New generate-ledger CLI verb with the exact four-positional-argument usage and exit-code mapping fixed in docs/contracts/ledger-generation-report.md

Valid, invalid, and golden fixtures under fixtures/ledger-generation/** covering: deliverables-only source, required_contract_decisions-only source, required_invariants-only source, both categories present, both categories empty (fail-closed), a non-string/empty entry in a source array, a missing/empty traceId argument, an unreadable task-contract path, malformed task-contract JSON, and byte-reproducibility across two generations of the same input
Conformance tests asserting exact diagnostic code and pointer for every PT600-PT606 condition and byte-identical regeneration output
README and CI usage updates limited to this verb and contract
Self-check evidence listing exact commands, fixture counts, changed paths, frozen-path verification (byte-identical protected_paths against main), and unresolved items
non_goals: No change of any kind to contracts/obligation-ledger.schema.json, docs/contracts/obligation-ledger.md, or any other existing Phase 0-4.2 contract, schema, diagnostic code, or CLI verb behavior
No parsing or semantic interpretation of objective, acceptance_commands, or any task-contract field other than deliverables, required_contract_decisions, and required_invariants
No signal, event, AgentSession, or GateOutcome attachment; no invocation of evaluate
No Phase B cross-document referential validation at generation time
No general document-to-obligation converter, ingestion adapter, or OpenTelemetry/framework-generic compatibility claim
No persistence, hosted service, UI, network calls, or automatic agent interruption
No cryptographic attestation implementation from ADR-0006
No synthetic benchmark expansion, threshold tuning, or changes to fixtures/benchmarks or annotations
stop_conditions: Implementation would require any diff to contracts/obligation-ledger.schema.json, docs/contracts/obligation-ledger.md, or any other protected contract
A required field can only be populated by free-text interpretation of objective, acceptance_commands, or an invented default
The generator would need to infer or synthesize traceId rather than receive it as an explicit argument
The generator would need to run Phase B referential validation or attach signals to satisfy a requirement
Two different candidate obligations in the same generation run cannot be given distinct stable ids without departing from the fixed id algorithm
Existing Phase 0-4.2 fixtures, schemas, CLI behavior, or deterministic semantics regress
The allowed path set is exceeded
